rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 8 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without being excessively steep. This should reveal whether any peaks are unretained, whether late compounds need strong elution, and where to focus subsequent narrowing or slope changes.

All peaks elute between about phi_e 0.20 and 0.44, so narrowing the gradient window around that region should greatly reduce gradient steepness and focus separation where the critical pair sits. Keep tG and T unchanged to isolate the effect of the phi window on the unresolved 4/5 pair.

The narrowed window substantially improved the critical 4/5 pair, so now make the gradient shallower to test whether that pair is slope-responsive enough to reach baseline resolution. Keeping the same phi window and temperature isolates the effect of tG on the unresolved pair.

The critical pair is strongly slope-responsive and nearly resolved at tG 30, but the time penalty is too high, so increase temperature one step to shorten the run while preserving the favorable shallow gradient. This also probes whether modest T selectivity can push the 4/5 pair over 1.5 without sacrificing too much resolution elsewhere.

The pair around rows 4/5 at 40 C became nearly resolved with shallower slope, while 45 C changed selectivity and shifted the bottleneck to a different close pair, so test one step lower in temperature with an intermediate tG to balance selectivity and runtime. This targets full resolution near the 40 C behavior but with less time penalty than tG 30.

Temperature clearly changes selectivity, and 45 C gave the best near-baseline overall pattern; lowering phi0 should spread the early-mid cluster more without making the gradient much steeper than the successful narrowed-window runs. This specifically targets the new critical 3/4 pair while keeping the last peak in a manageable range.

At 45 C the bottleneck is the early-mid 3/4 pair, so raise phi1 one step to shift the effective phi range upward and alter selectivity around that cluster while also shortening the late part of the run. This tests whether the close pair responds more to phi window placement than to further slope changes.

Injection 7 is close to optimal: only the 3/4 pair is slightly below full credit and the time penalty is already small. Lengthening the gradient by one step should selectively improve that pair with only a modest increase in t_last, likely giving a net CRF gain.

The close 3/4 pair barely improved with a longer gradient, suggesting it is not strongly slope-responsive here; instead, shift the gradient window upward one more step to probe selectivity changes around that pair while keeping the efficient runtime of injection 7. A higher phi1 should also reduce the small time penalty if selectivity is preserved or improved.

Injection 9 is excellent and already avoids any time penalty, so the only possible gain is pushing the 3/4 pair to full resolution credit through another small upward shift of the phi window. Since slope changes had little effect on that pair, this is the most direct selectivity probe while keeping runtime safely under 10 minutes.

Injection 9 appears near the optimum window; raising phi1 further created a new unresolved late pair, so keep phi1 at 0.55 and instead raise phi0 one step to shift the window upward and test selectivity on the stubborn 3/4 pair without over-compressing the late peaks. This should also retain the no-penalty runtime region.

The best current method is injection 9, and the stubborn 3/4 pair has responded more to selectivity than to slope, so keep that successful window and probe temperature one step higher. This may reorder or further separate the close pair while likely keeping t_last below 10 minutes.

Higher temperature sharply worsened the critical pair, so probe one step lower than the current optimum while keeping the successful window fixed. This is the cleanest remaining selectivity test to see whether the 3/4 pair can be pushed above 1.5 without incurring a time penalty.

The best region remains centered on injection 9, but changing phi0 and phi1 in opposite directions has not yet been tested there; lowering phi0 one step while keeping phi1 at 0.55 expands the window and shifts extra resolving power toward the early cluster containing the stubborn close pair. This is a targeted check for whether the 3/4 pair benefits from a slightly broader, lower-start gradient without sacrificing the late peaks.

Injection 9 is still the best and already has no time penalty, but shortening tG by one step may preserve the same nearly full resolution while reducing run time further; even if CRF cannot exceed 0.987 much, this checks whether the current method is on the shortest plateau. It also confirms whether the stubborn 3/4 pair is essentially insensitive to a modest slope increase in the optimum window.

At the current best window, 40 C and 50 C both strongly changed selectivity, so one more temperature point at 55 C is worthwhile because the close pair appears dominated by selectivity rather than slope. This is a high-information test of whether a different thermal selectivity regime can finally push the limiting pair above 1.5 while still keeping the run fast.

The best method likely sits near the 45 C, phi0 0.25, phi1 0.50–0.55 region, but the remaining limiting pair may benefit from moving the whole window slightly lower rather than higher. Testing 0.20–0.50 keeps a similar slope to successful runs while probing a distinct selectivity placement for the early-mid critical cluster.

The 0.25–0.50 window was promising at 45 C, and temperature has shown strong selectivity effects; testing 50 C here could improve the stubborn 3/4 pair differently than it did at 0.25–0.55 because the phi window placement also changes selectivity. This is a targeted cross-check in the only other near-optimal window family.

At 40 C the selectivity pattern changed to different critical pairs, so combining that temperature with a slightly shallower gradient may recover those pairs and reveal whether 40 C can become competitive when slope is adjusted. This is a targeted check of the only remaining plausible route to surpass injection 9 by changing both selectivity and slope together.

Most evidence points to 45 C as best, but 35 C has not been tested in the best phi window and may offer a distinct selectivity regime for the stubborn close pair. Using tG 26 gives that lower-temperature selectivity a fair chance by adding a bit of resolving power while keeping the experiment close to the known optimum region.

With five injections left and no condition surpassing injection 9, test the one remaining adjacent window around it that balances the failures at 0.20–0.55 and 0.25–0.60. This broader, slightly lower-start/higher-end window may relieve the stubborn 3/4 pair without creating the severe late-pair compression seen at 0.25–0.60.

The unresolved pair near injection 9 behaves largely selectivity-limited, but a larger slope change has not been tested in the best window itself; 26 min was unavailable there, so try 28 min as the remaining meaningful slope probe. If the 3/4 pair can cross 1.5 while t_last stays close to 10 min, this is the most plausible route left to beat the current best.

The 0.25–0.55, 45 C window is clearly the optimum region, and the small change from 22 to 24 min had little effect on the critical pair, suggesting a broad plateau. Testing 20 min checks whether the same near-maximal resolution can be kept with a still shorter method, which could match or potentially exceed the current best if no new pair collapses.

With only two shots left, test the last nearby window not yet explored around the best method by broadening both ends symmetrically. This may redistribute selectivity enough to improve the persistent 3/4 pair while avoiding the late-pair collapse seen at 0.25–0.60.

For the final shot, push the window one more step lower at the start while keeping the higher end that preserved late-peak spacing, targeting extra expansion of the early-mid critical cluster that consistently limits CRF. This is the last untested neighboring window around the best 45 C region with a realistic chance of improving the stubborn 3/4 pair without causing a new late-pair collapse.
